paper_title: VisuoThink Empowering LVLM Reasoning with Multimodal Tree Search
caption: (LEFT) The trend of Pass@1 rate on Visual Navigation as the number of reasoning steps increases. (right) The relationship between the Accuracy@1 on geometry problems (Geomverse) and tree width for rollout search. We observe that LVLMs significantly benefit from longer reasoning chains, although the effect plateaus rapidly beyond a certain threshold of reasoning steps. The relationship between performance and tree width exhibits a more complex pattern, demonstrating an inverted U-shaped trend with both GPT-4o and Claude-3.5-Sonnet.
model_annotation: The plot illustrates how Pass@1 Rate changes on a visual navigation task as the number of reasoning steps increases, with two model series shown. The x-axis is labeled “Num. of Reasoning Steps,” uses a linear scale, and spans from 5 to 40 with labeled ticks at 5, 10, 20, and 40. The y-axis is labeled “Pass@1 Rate (%)”, uses a linear scale, and ranges from 0 to 100 with labeled ticks at 0, 20, 40, 60, 80, and 100. One line corresponds to GPT-4o, drawn as a solid blue line with filled circular markers; it rises from 6.5 at 5 steps to 32.3 at 10 steps, increases further to 77.4 at 20 steps, and reaches 83.9 at 40 steps. The second line corresponds to Claude-3.5-Sonnet, drawn as a solid light-blue line with “x” markers; it increases from 19.4 at 5 steps to 38.7 at 10 steps, then to 87.1 at 20 steps, and to 89.2 at 40 steps.
